title: PolicyLayer
description: One layer of a run's policy (R2 CP3, 02-lld §2.4): a partial document, every section optional, at one scope of the precedence chain. Each value is a dimension of policy-dimensions.json: a ceiling narrows the layers above it, a choice picks inside its ceiling, an operator row is set by the deployment only. A layer names a dimension by setting it; nothing in a layer is null.

approvals.description: Per-call approval rules (P2.6c, P2.11e); layers meet as the strictest of them.

memory.description: The org's governed-memory policy (P7.3). Not a dimension yet: Node reads it at admission and settlement.

retention.description: How long the org's conversations are kept before they are erased (E7). Not a dimension: the retention sweeper reads it.

locks.description: Dimensions this layer locks (C4.02): a layer below may not set a locked choice or operator row to another value, nor widen a locked ceiling (refused as `locked`, naming the dimension and the layer that tried). A locked ceiling may still be narrowed: a stricter value never overrides the admin's limit. A layer below carries the lock's authority for a section its `lockedBy` gives to the locking layer or one above it. Each entry is a row of policy-dimensions.json this layer may set.

lockedBy.description: Sections of this layer owned by a layer above it (02-lld §11.1: an org's rules for an agent sit in the agent layer, locked by the org, so the agent's builder cannot remove an admin's asks). Section name → the layer whose admins write it; such a section carries that layer's authority over a dimension it `locks` (C4.02).

updated.description: Who last saved each section and when (shown to editors; not policy, never resolved).

snapshots.description: How long engine sandbox snapshots are kept (OWD-12).

triggers.description: Webhook limits and where completion notices may go, for scheduled and triggered runs (TR-04, TR-07).

websites.description: Allowed websites (WP-63, C6.11, C11.04): the named sites an agent's sandbox may reach through the egress proxy, https only. Off by default: absent at the org, no site is reachable. Not a dimension: the worker folds the deployment's, the org's and the agent's sections from the org's live layer at each engine turn. The deployment's section caps what any org may list; an org's lists its sites; an agent's may only narrow its org's (fewer sites, narrower paths, read for read-write), never widen. Absent at the deployment: no cap; absent at an agent: its org's sites.

repositories.description: Allowed git hosts for repository_fetch (WP-63 part A): the hosts whose public repositories an agent may ask to clone, each clone approved by a person and fetched by the worker outside the sandbox, never with a credential. Absent at the org: the release's default presets (github.com, gitlab.com and bitbucket.org public repositories) on a run with web access, none without it (ADR-REPO-01); a saved section, even an empty one, replaces them. Not a dimension: the worker folds the org's and the agent's sections from the org's live layer at each call. An org's lists hosts, optionally limited to owner or owner/repo prefixes; an agent's may only narrow its org's. Absent at an agent: its org's hosts.

quotas.description: Concurrency caps per org and per person (C4.10).

toolResults.description: The inline tool-result cap and the response_format default (C4.10).

interactions.description: How long a run waits for a person and whether an answer may cover the conversation (C4.10).

recovery.description: Whether a run whose worker was lost resumes (C4.10).

ui.description: What a conversation shows: reasoning and the terminal (C4.10).

access.description: Who may use the harness, each coding engine and each configured model, as the org's user groups (G-41, GA-21; the groups an IdP or SCIM sync would write). Org layer only, saved and read by org admins only. Not a dimension: admission re-reads the actor's live group membership at every admission and readmission (submit, the next-run drain, schedules and triggers), so a removal refuses the next run at once; a run already admitted runs to its end. Absent, or a subject left out: no group restriction on it. A listed subject admits a member of any of its groups; org admins are not exempt.

LayerName.description: A layer of the precedence chain (02-lld §3.1), top to bottom.

ModelRoute.description: A model the run may call, as the deployment names its configured models.

ModelPolicy.description: Which models a run may call (`routes`, a ceiling) and which it calls (`primary`, and one per named sub-agent role in `roles`), each inside `routes`; `roleCostCeilings` bounds what a role's model may cost (MA1). `disabledRules` and `consumerPlans` are the org's narrowing of the vendor rules (A1): rules it switched off, and whether consumer plans may be used.

roleCostCeilings.description: The most a sub-agent role's model may cost, USD per 1M tokens (input plus output list price); `default` bounds every role.

RolloutPolicy.description: Features as the Labs settings switch them per org (flags.json `labs` rows), which turns take the durable path (`durable`), and whether the org's capabilities are migrated to the control plane; a deployment may hold one off for every org.

DurableRollout.description: Which turns take the durable path (CPD-10): each list narrows the release's; a turn outside one stays on today's loop.

modelFamilies.description: Model families (the configured model's provider, lower-case); an empty list admits none.

OperatorPolicy.description: Operator-only settings (R2 §2.3): the deployment layer sets them from env and Helm values; no layer below may.

SANDBOX_MODE.description: The sandbox backend (flags.json lists its values).

BudgetPolicy.description: Run budgets (CPD-5): ceilings a layer narrows; an engine profile's limits narrow the same values (budgets and engine limits are one dimension). null is unbounded.

CatalogPolicy.description: Configuration-time policy for catalog items (02-lld §2.4): who approves a change and what an org delegates to team admins. Dimensions `catalog.approval`, `catalog.delegation`.

approval.description: Approver per change rule `{change}:{kind}`; `*` stands for every kind.

delegation.description: Actions a team's admins may take on the team's own objects.

ApproverLevel.description: Who approves, from the loosest up. An edition's overlay may add stricter levels after these.

DelegableAction.description: A control-plane action an org may delegate to team admins.

ToolDisclosureMode.description: How a run's tools reach the model (checklist §5): eager lists every granted tool; lazy lists the most-used and finds the rest through search_tools and call_tool; filesystem lists the meta tools only and describes every tool in /pipeshub/tools (engines; the native loop reads it as lazy).

ToolDisclosurePolicy.description: Tool disclosure (C5.01): `modes` the org allows (a ceiling), `mode` the agent's pick inside it (a choice). Unset, each executor keeps its own default (the native loop lazy above PIPESHUB_LAZY_TOOLS_THRESHOLD tools, an engine above PIPESHUB_ENGINE_LAZY_TOOLS_THRESHOLD).

SnapshotTtlDays.description: Days an engine sandbox snapshot is kept (OWD-12).

SnapshotPolicy.description: Engine sandbox snapshots (OWD-12): `ttlDays` how long one is kept. A snapshot older than its org's ttlDays is deleted by the retention sweeper and never restored.

WriteAction.description: The kinds of external write an identity is chosen for (OWD-18).

NotifyChannel.description: Where a schedule's actor is told that a run ended (TR-07).

WebhookMaxBytes.description: The largest webhook trigger body accepted, in bytes (TR-04).

WebhookPerMinute.description: Authenticated deliveries a webhook trigger takes per minute (TR-04).

TriggerPolicy.description: Triggers (TR-04, TR-07): `webhookMaxBytes` and `webhookPerMinute` bound what one webhook trigger takes; `notifyChannels` where completion notices may go.

WebsitePolicy.description: A layer's allowed websites; an empty list allows none.

orgOnlyAddresses.description: Addresses only this organization can reach (WP83-FU-3): host names (intranet.acme.com, or *.corp.acme.com for its subdomains), IP addresses or CIDR ranges that answer only the organization's own callers, such as an IP-allowlisted intranet or a self-hosted git server on a public address. Content fetched from them (a fetch_url page, a repository_fetch clone) is never treated as public, so a later send outside the organization still asks. Set at the org layer only; absent: none. PipesHub never probes an address from outside to decide this.

AllowedWebsite.description: One allowed website: a host name, or *. and a domain for its subdomains (never a public suffix such as *.com or *.github.io), reached over https on port 443. Never an IP address, a private or metadata name, PipesHub's own host, or a git host (github.com, gitlab.com...).

host.description: Lower-case host name, or *.domain for every subdomain of domain (not domain itself).

readWriteConfirmed.description: Set when an admin confirmed read-write access; required for read-write, absent for read.

paths.description: Path prefixes the site is limited to (docs.example.com /api/ for its API reference); absent: the whole site. A prefix matches itself and what follows it after a slash.

opaque.description: Host-level only: the proxy cannot inspect this site (a pinned client, an internal mirror), so it opens an opaque tunnel and the agent can send data to it. Read-write only, never a read-only-listed host or a preset's host.

preset.description: The preset this entry was added from (shown to admins); it grants nothing by itself.

note.description: Why the site is allowed, shown to admins and in the agent's instructions.

WebsiteAccess.description: read: GET, HEAD and OPTIONS only. read-write: every method; an admin confirms it. Neither is ever git: a git host is never a website, and git's smart-HTTP is refused at every site.

RepositoryPolicy.description: A layer's allowed git hosts; an empty list allows none.

AllowedRepositoryHost.description: One git host whose public repositories may be cloned over https (port 443): a host name, never a wildcard, an IP address, a private or metadata name or PipesHub's own host.

prefixes.description: Owner or owner/repo prefixes the host is limited to (acme/ for one owner, acme/widgets for one repository); absent: every public repository on the host.

publicReadable.description: Whether anyone on the internet can read this host's public repositories (WP83-FU-3). Off (absent) for a host an admin adds by hand, so a clone from it is never treated as public and a later send outside the organization asks. An entry added from a repository preset (github-public) is public-readable whatever this says.

preset.description: The repository preset this entry was added from (github-public); it grants nothing by itself.

note.description: Why the host is allowed, shown to admins.

QuotaPolicy.description: Concurrency caps (C4.10, P1.14): `activeRunsPerOrg` and `activeRunsPerUser` bound the runs queued or running at once.

ActiveRunsPerOrg.description: Runs one org may have queued or running at once.

ActiveRunsPerUser.description: Runs one person may have queued or running at once.

ResponseFormat.description: How much a knowledge search returns (WP-12): concise or detailed.

ToolResultMaxChars.description: Characters of one tool result the model reads inline (C4.10).

ToolResultPolicy.description: Tool results (C4.10): `maxChars` the inline cap (null: each executor's own); `formats` the response_format values allowed, `format` the default.

PersonWaitS.description: Seconds a run waits for a person's answer (C4.10).

InteractionPolicy.description: Approvals and questions (C4.10): `waitS` how long a run waits for an answer (null: the deployment's); `conversationGrants` whether an answer may cover the rest of the conversation.

RecoveryPolicy.description: Crash recovery (C4.10): `autoResume` whether a run whose worker was lost resumes from its checkpoint.

SandboxResourcePolicy.description: An engine run's sandbox resources (C4.10): each lowers the engine template's value, never raises it; null: the template's; inputMaxMb lowers the deployment's largest input (J-26).

UiPolicy.description: What a conversation shows (C4.10): `reasoning` the model's reasoning, `terminal` an engine run's read-only terminal.

AccessGroupIds.description: Org user group ids; a member of any of them is admitted.

harness.description: Who may start harness runs (agent chats, the assistant's Agent mode, schedules and triggers). Someone outside them keeps classic chat where a turn can fall back to it.

engines.description: Coding engine kind (`claude_code`, `codex`, `opencode`) → the groups that may use it. Someone outside them gets no hand-off to that engine; the turn still runs.

models.description: Configured model key (an AI models entry) → the groups that may run on it. A turn on a model whose groups do not include the actor is refused; the org default counts as the entry it resolves to.

OrgOnlyAddress.description: A lower-case host name, *. and a domain for every subdomain of it, an IP address, or a CIDR range (10.20.0.0/16, 2001:db8::/32).
